subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should this issue be narrowed to a safe read-tool fallback for known binary documents, or should it wait for broader native document extraction/provider-file work?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the issue proposes both a lightweight warning and automatic parsing; parsing changes security and dependency boundaries while the safe fallback is a smaller product behavior choice.

options.title: Narrow to safe fallback
options.body: Implement bounded MIME/extension detection in the shared read path and return a clear message for known binary document formats, leaving parsing to existing PDF and linked document work.

options.title: Fold into document extraction
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader Office/document extraction and provider-native file design instead of changing read behavior independently.

options.title: Defer core behavior
options.body: Leave the read tool unchanged and rely on existing tools/plugins until maintainers approve a document handling boundary.

recommendation.title: Narrow to safe fallback
recommendation.body: Implement bounded MIME/extension detection in the shared read path and return a clear message for known binary document formats, leaving parsing to existing PDF and linked document work.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history on the read-wrapper boundary and broad product-routing evidence for core-versus-plugin decisions.
